entries.title: Cà de Bezzi, Bolzano: postcard of the Batzenhäusl with its German names blacked out

facts: Touriseum inv. 4090261, publisher 'R. & R. D.', series 2363, '(datiert) 1902': 'Die Beschriftung war ursprünglich deutsch und italienisch. Die deutsche Bezeichnung wurde durchgestrichen'; keywords 'Kutsche Italianisierung', place 'Bozen' (record)

entries.title: Bollettino Ufficiale della Prefettura di Bolzano, 16 October 1927, pages 161–162: “Uso della lingua italiana”, circular n. 6480
facts: Prefect Umberto Ricci's circular 11 Oct 1927 n. 6480 Gab. quotes the decree of the Prefect of the Venezia Tridentina of 28 Oct 1923 n. 14718: all 'insegne, etichette … tutte le scritte e leggende … anche se concernono interessi privati' only in Italian; a German translation, where allowed, 'in caratteri latini di non maggiore dimensione e appariscenza' (notes 18, §1, [V])

German lettering to be 'cancellate con raschiatura e coloritura radicali'; the podestà must not accept 'la semplice cancellatura della parte redatta in lingua tedesca, senza preoccuparsi dello squilibrio, anche estetico'; bilingual signs 'dovranno essere totalmente rinnovate' (notes 18, §1, [V])

Bilingual lettering still allowed only in Appiano, Bolzano (with Oltrisarco and Gries), Bressanone, Caldaro, Lana and Merano; deadline 30 Nov 1927; tableware, linen and glasses with German until 30 Nov 1929; house names in German included (notes 18, §1, [V])
This is the decree on private signs that notes 16 (§1, Gaps) did not find (notes 18, §1)
Seen in the image (p. 161): two columns under 'Comunicazioni varie'; the circular begins in the left column; a reader's pen brackets its heading and the passage on 'semplice cancellatura'
Seen in the image (p. 162): the end of the circular with underlinings, Ricci's signature, the 'Modello di Avviso' for the podestà, and a further circular

entries.title: Bollettino Ufficiale della Prefettura di Bolzano, 16 November 1927, page 173: decree on “corretto uso della lingua italiana” and circular n. 7622 on funeral inscriptions
facts: Decree of 3 Nov 1927 (sent with circular n. 7308 of 4 Nov): every notice, sign or label for the public to be submitted to the commune in draft and corrected to 'corretta lezione italiana'; offenders reported under art. 434 of the penal code (notes 18, §1, [V])

Circular 16 Nov 1927 n. 7622: 'le inscrizioni funebri debbono essere redatte nella sola lingua italiana unicamente quando siano posteriori al giorno 30 settembre c. a. Le scritte anteriori non debbono, quindi, essere cancellate o sostituite'; German inscriptions 'di carattere storico ed artistico' decided case by case; hotels may ask for four languages on interior signs (notes 18, §1, [V])

Answers the gravestone question of notes 16 §1 and row 16.13; contradicts the Kastelruth announcement reported in Innsbruck on 15 Nov 1927 that old grave inscriptions had to be replaced by 30 Nov (notes 18, §6)
Seen in the image: p. 173 under 'Parte ufficiale – Comunicazioni varie'; the decree in the left column; the circular on funeral inscriptions at right, its key sentence underlined in pen

entries.title: Der Südtiroler (Innsbruck), 1 December 1934, page 6: “Meran ist deutsch”

facts: One line per OMA record whose description reports a German name covered, struck, blacked, pasted over or replaced on the object, plus the 1919 station photographs and three comparison records (manifest)

38 Touriseum, 32 Palais Mamming, 2 Pharmaziemuseum Brixen, 2 Stadtarchiv Brixen; 54 postcards (19 of the Mamming ones untyped in the portal), 13 photographs, 2 brochures, an album, two pharmacy objects, a map of 1960–80, a passport of 1919 (notes 18, §2)
Rows 18.01–18.20 hold 15 of these records; the column 'held_as_row' says which (manifest)
